insights.headline: Gold steadies near $4,010 into Fed week as the rupee's slide adds to import costs
insights.summary: Spot gold held near $4,010 an ounce on Monday after a more than 4% weekly fall, its steepest since June, while silver traded near $54 after breaking below its July low. MCX gold December futures recovered to about ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams and silver to about ₹1.96 lakh per kg. The rupee closed at 95.1850 per dollar, its third straight fall, adding to the landed cost of bullion. With the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting ahead, festive buyers face lower prices into Dhanteras, though analysts caution bullion stays under pressure until the policy path clears.
points: Spot gold near $4,010 after a 4% weekly fall; silver near $54 after breaking its July low.
MCX gold December futures around ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams; silver near ₹1.96 lakh per kg.
The rupee closed at 95.1850 per dollar, down a third straight session on importer demand and foreign outflows.
The Fed's October 27-28 meeting and Thursday's PCE data are the week's key triggers.
HSBC sees limited near-term gains for silver even after the slide; UBS keeps a $70 view.

trending.title: Fed week takes centre stage
trending.summary: The October 27-28 FOMC meeting and Thursday's PCE data dominate bullion, with a December hike now priced near 75%.

trending.title: Silver's slide puts $50 in focus
trending.summary: Silver's two-week slide has outpaced gold's, breaking below $54 and its July low, with $50 now the level traders are watching.

trending.title: Festive buying meets lower prices
trending.summary: Gold's pullback lands just ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali, giving festive buyers lower prices but no clear all-clear from analysts.

trending.title: Rupee slides a third session
trending.summary: Importer dollar demand, crude near $115 and foreign outflows pushed the rupee to 95.1850, lifting the landed cost of bullion imports.

trending.title: Central banks split as demand broadens
trending.summary: Central banks are divided, with Russia selling and China buying, even as gold's demand base broadens below $4,000.

items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.4% to $4,009.87 an ounce on Monday as softer oil prices eased inflation worries, after a 4% weekly fall, its steepest in more than four months, ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting. FXEmpire notes gold trades below a falling trendline, with CME FedWatch pricing about a 75% chance of at least one Fed hike by December; silver held near $54.20 after touching $53.43.
items.title: Gold (XAUUSD) & Silver Price Forecast: Gold Steadies Into Fed Week as Hike Odds Hit 75%, Can Gold Hold $3,946?
Gold News: XAUUSD Gets Fed-Week Relief, but Inflation Keeps Bears in Control
items.summary: Gold edged higher ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting, but FXEmpire's read stays bearish: December hike odds and upcoming PCE inflation data keep resistance overhead, and the metal's broader downtrend remains intact despite the Fed-week relief.

Spot gold slipped 0.1% to $3,993.20 an ounce in Singapore trading on Monday after falling more than 4% last week, its biggest weekly drop since June, as traders weighed high energy prices ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting. Silver climbed 0.5% to $54.12 after giving up 5.4% last week, while markets priced only about a 10% chance of a Fed hike this week.
items.title: Gold steadies after weekly drop as focus shifts to Fed meeting
Why is gold price under pressure ahead of Dhanteras, Diwali? What should interested buyers do? Experts's views, target
items.summary: Mint examines why gold is under pressure ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali, with experts linking the pullback to a stronger dollar, elevated bond yields and oil-driven inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting. The metal's weekly fall left MCX gold near ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams as festive buying approaches.

MCX gold December futures opened ₹277 higher at ₹1,42,301 per 10 grams on Monday and traded at ₹1,42,500, up 0.34%, after last week's near-4% slide, while silver December futures traded at ₹1,95,572 per kg after an intraday high of ₹1,97,186. Experts cited by IANS said gold needs to reclaim ₹1,43,000-₹1,43,700 to stabilise, with silver facing resistance at ₹2,00,000-₹2,02,000.
items.title: Gold, silver bounce back after sharp sell-off, but yellow metal near 3-month low
Gold gains on softer oil prices; Fed decision in focus
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.4% to $4,009.87 an ounce on Monday as softer oil prices eased inflation worries, after bullion hit its lowest since mid-July and fell 4% last week. US December gold futures gained 0.4% to $4,023.50, while spot silver rose 0.6% to $54.19. Markets now await the Federal Reserve's October 28 policy meeting and PCE inflation data due the next day.

items.title: Rupee weakens for third session as importers step up dollar bids, foreign outflows bite
items.summary: The rupee closed at 95.1850 per dollar on Monday, down 0.3% on the day and about 0.8% over three sessions, as importer dollar demand, Brent crude near $115 a barrel and foreign outflows weighed. Traders noted the absence of recent RBI dollar sales that had supported the currency; a weaker rupee raises the landed cost of dollar-priced bullion for Indian buyers.

items.title: Silver prices are tarnished but not forgotten. Why HSBC thinks gains in white metal may be limited?
items.summary: Silver prices are tarnished but not forgotten, the Economic Times reports, as HSBC argues gains in the white metal may be limited even after its sharp slide from recent highs. The cautious view lands as silver trades near $54 after breaking below its July low, with investors watching whether $50 holds.

items.title: Silver's Two-Week Slide More Than Doubles Gold's—Could $50 Hold?
items.summary: Silver has fallen 11.5% since October 9, more than double gold's 4.7% drop, pushing the gold/silver ratio to 75.11 after silver broke below its July low of $54.77. ActionForex puts $50 in focus, with $52.53 next, and notes silver traded near $54.06 on Monday while gold held near $4,014. India's approval of about 6,500 tonnes of silver imports has coincided with lower premiums and subdued demand.

items.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD gains at start of Fed's policy week
items.summary: Gold found buyers below $4,000 in Asian trading on Monday as the Federal Reserve's policy week began, though it stayed close to its three-month low of $3,975. Markets widely expect the Fed to hold rates in the 3.75%-4.00% range, making the policy guidance the key near-term catalyst, with recent remarks from Fed officials pointing to more persistent inflation and the possibility of further hikes.

items.title: Silver's Physical Market Goes Quiet While UBS Keeps Its $70 Bet Alive
items.summary: Silver fell 5.7% over seven days to $53.96 as buyers and sellers held back ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting, ad-hoc-news reports. Physical trading has gone quiet even as UBS kept its $70 target for December 2026, leaving the metal caught between a soft spot market and a still-constructive bank forecast.

items.title: Bullion outlook hinges on Fed as oil fuels inflation fears
items.summary: MCX gold futures for December fell Rs 5,768, or nearly 4%, over the past week to close at Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, while silver slid 7.14% to Rs 1.96 lakh per kg, below Rs 2 lakh. Analysts cited surging crude oil, elevated bond yields and a stronger dollar, with the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, US PCE data and third-quarter GDP now the key cues for bullion.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD slips below $54.00 amid easing safe-haven demand
items.summary: Silver slipped below $54 an ounce in Asian trading, around $53.70, as safe-haven demand eased after US President Donald Trump ruled out an immediate strike on Iran. Elevated energy prices kept expectations of higher-for-longer rates in focus, and traders now await the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, with CME FedWatch pricing a 90.6% chance of a pause.

items.title: How can people lock low gold prices now to buy jewellery a week later on Dhanteras?
items.summary: With gold down sharply in recent days to Rs 1,41,630 per 10 grams on IBJA data ahead of Dhanteras, experts cited by Inshorts say buyers can book jewellery now and lock in the current rate, then take delivery on Dhanteras. Advance booking lets shoppers use the dip without waiting until the festival day itself.

items.title: 5 things happening in the gold market ahead of Diwali and Dhanteras 2026, as per WGC
items.summary: The World Gold Council's latest India update, 'Seasonal demand shows early strength', says prices steadied after September's sharp fall and domestic discounts narrowed from $66 an ounce in September to $8 by October 16 as festive and wedding-season demand built. Demand is strengthening into Diwali and Dhanteras, though the Council cautions high prices may still cap volumes.

items.title: Gold's Demand Base Is Broadening Even as Prices Slip Below $4,000
items.summary: Gold closed Friday at $3,997.48, below $4,000 for the first time since mid-July, in its steepest weekly loss in over four months — yet demand signals point the other way. Speculators cut net-long gold futures by 8,014 to 199,865, while China added 23 tonnes in September, Indian gold ETFs drew ₹17.22 billion in early October, and Goldman Sachs put August central-bank buying at 79 tonnes.

items.title: Central banks split over gold: Russia is selling, China is buying
items.summary: China stretched its gold-buying streak to a 23rd straight month with a 740,000-ounce September purchase, its largest since September 2023, while Russia has sold 56 tonnes this year, World Gold Council data show. Poland, the year's biggest buyer, and Kazakhstan sit on the buying side of a split that shows official demand is far from one-directional even as prices correct.

items.title: Silver price has broken below ₹2 lakh for the first time since December 2025: Is this the right time to buy for returns?
items.summary: Silver fell to ₹1,92,800 per kg on MCX on Friday, its first close below ₹2 lakh since December 2025, after losing about ₹6,800 in a session. It is down 22.5% from its August peak of ₹2,48,800 and over 50% below January's ₹4,20,048 record. Augmont's Renisha Chainani put $50–$55 as a support zone, with a possible 10–15% rebound ahead.

items.title: Gold, Silver Prices Dip But Many Gold ETF FoFs Temporarily Halt Fresh Inflows: What Are Your Options?
items.summary: Gold slipped nearly Rs 1,700 to about Rs 1,44,340 per 10 grams and silver fell below Rs 2 lakh per kg ahead of Diwali and Dhanteras, pressured by Middle East tensions and US rate expectations. Since October 16, several fund houses have temporarily stopped fresh investments into gold ETF fund-of-funds, while existing SIPs continue and gold ETFs bought directly on the exchanges remain open.

items.title: Senco Gold to acquire 68% stake in August Jewellery for ₹68 crore
items.summary: Senco Gold has signed definitive agreements to buy a 68% stake in August Jewellery, the company behind online jewellery brand Melorra, for ₹68 crore in tranches. With a promoter-group entity also investing, the total holding will reach 79% and August Jewellery will become a Senco subsidiary, with completion targeted by February 2027.

items.title: Gold Price Surge From 2022 To 2026: What Fueled The Rise In 5 Years And Why Are Prices Falling Today? Check Year-by-Year Comparison
items.summary: Gold has fallen to about $4,000 an ounce, nearly 29% below its January peak of $5,595, after climbing from a 2022 average of $1,802. On October 25, retail 24K gold in India stood at ₹1,42,580 per 10 grams and MCX December futures at ₹1,42,150, down 0.81%. The pullback is attributed to a stronger dollar, oil-driven inflation, higher-for-longer US rate expectations and profit-booking.
